title: Brain Registration and Evaluation for Zebrafish (BREEZE)-mapping: A pipeline for whole-brain structural and activity analyses
protocol: Organize confocal microscope files in preparation for pre-processing.
Create a tif subfolder containing all .tif files.
Create an nrrd subfolder containing all .nrrd files.
Create an optfixed subfolder containing .nii ("optfixed") files.
Visualize maximum projections of all z-stack images prior to registration using ImageJ scripts.
Convert whole-brain confocal z-stack images (.lif files) to max projection files (.tif) and converted images (.nrrd) in the correct orientation for registration.
Open the script File → Open → max_nrrd_2.ijm or max_nrrd_3.ijm → Run.

Input folder locations of images as prompted in the following sequence: lif (location of .lif files) → tif (folder for max projection .tif files to be created) → nrrd (folder for .nrrd files to be created).
The script will generate a max projection image and prompt the user to rotate the image to the optimal orientation.
Rotate the image to anterior (forebrain) facing up using options from the drop-down menu: 0 = no rotation; 1 = 90 degrees clockwise; 2 = 180 degrees clockwise; 3 = 270 degrees clockwise.
Verify that a .nrrd file is generated 90 degrees clockwise to the orientation of the .tif for registration purposes, with anterior facing right.
Ensure the acquisition orientation matches your dataset/microscope requirements.
Visualize all confocal images as max projections to assess image quality.
Run summary_2.js, summary_3.js from the pre-processing folder.
Create a new template in Adobe Illustrator (any size template; Color Mode: RGB).
Open the script in Adobe Illustrator (File → Scripts → Other Scripts).
The script will prompt the user to open the tif folder containing the max projection files.
The script will automatically display the max projection images organized by genotype on the template.
Check image quality and exclude samples with obvious inconsistencies in dissecting, staining, or mounting.
Exclude samples that are excessively rotated, damaged, or inconsistently stained from analysis.
Open the BioImage Suite Web App.
Navigate to “Help” and select “Enable Internal Feature.”
Navigate to “Image Processing” and select “Fix Zebrafish Images.”
Set RAS and resample parameters in the side bar.
Unselect biascorrect, normalize, and mask parameters.
Set Smooth sigma = 1 and Resample Factor = 1.
Load each nrrd file individually in Bioimage Suite Web.
Select “Execute” to process each image.
Save processed images as optfixed images (∗_optfixed.nii.gz).
Upload the optfixed folder containing all converted images to a dedicated experiment folder on an HPCC.
Change directories to the experiment folder containing the optfixed folder.
Execute reg.sh in the command line by entering bash reg.sh.
Reslice the image in each channel using BioImage Suite.
Align the pre-processed first cell-specific marker image with the standard reference brain.
Save the registered file for the first cell-specific marker image.
Align the pre-processed uniform marker image with the standard reference brain.
Save the registered file for the uniform marker image.
Align the pre-processed second cell-specific marker image with the standard reference brain.
Save the registered file for the second cell-specific marker image.
Normalize the intensity of the cell-specific label to the uniform label using reg.sh.
Divide the three-dimensional whole-brain z-stacks labeled with the cell-specific marker in the C0 or C2 channels by those labeled with the uniform marker in the C1 channel.
Use the -div option in the fslmaths command to divide the intensity value of each voxel in the cell-specific image by the intensity value of the corresponding voxel in the uniformly labeled image.
Generate a new file for each divided z-stack (r_*C0divC1.nii.gz) representing the voxel-by-voxel division.
mkdir -p divided/C0divC1
fslmaths ${registered_c0_file} -div ${registered_cl_file} divided/C0divC1/${divided_file}
mkdir -p divided/C2divC1
fslmaths ${registered_c2_file} -div ${registered_cl_file} divided/C2divC1/${divided_file}
Perform Jacobian calculation using the .bisxform transformation files.
reg.sh calculates the ratio between the test brain and a 2 × 2 × 2 resampled version of the standard reference brain using jacobianimage function.
Generate a mask_ja*.nii.gz file using a binary mask corresponding to brain regions in the Z-Brain atlas.
Use headerinfo tool to confirm that Jacobian calculations are performed on 2 × 2 × 2 resampled zebrafish standard reference brain (standard_ref_rsp.nii.gz).
Check reg.sh generated subfolders containing expected files: xform, registered, divided, and jacobian.
Quantify regional image intensities representing brain activity or other cell-specific markers.
Define regions of interest using zebrafish brain atlases for multiple fish in each experimental group.
Adapt the zebrafish brain atlas from Randlett et al. and Thyme et al. as described by Weinschutz Mendes et al.
Use a 4-region atlas (Zbrain_atlas_4region.nii.gz) to quantify phenotypes across four major subdivisions of the zebrafish brain: telencephalon, diencephalon, mesencephalon, and rhombencephalon.
Use an 8-region atlas (Zbrain_atlas_8region.nii.gz) to quantify phenotypes across eight major brain regions: forebrain (telencephalon), optic tectum, thalamus, hypothalamus, and cerebellum.
Type roi.sh in the terminal command line followed by the number designating the desired atlas.
Specify the bin folder in roi.sh.
Use the computeroi function of BioImage Suite in roi.sh.
Calculate average intensity values of the ratio of cell-specific marker to tERK within ROIs designated by the zebrafish brain atlas.
Deposit files in new roi_* subfolders named according to the atlas used and containing subfolders for each cell-specific marker.
Execute vol.sh script in the experiment folder to quantify regional differences in brain volume.
Generate .csv files containing average Jacobian values for each brain region based on the selected brain atlas using vol.sh.
Integrate Jacobian values for all fish into a combined dataset using vol.sh.
Load each image in BioImage Suite (File → Load Image).
Load the desired zebrafish brain atlas in the viewer as the “Objectmap” (Objectmap → Load Objectmap).
Perform a “VOI Analysis” (Objectmap → VOI Analysis) (“VOI” is used interchangeably with “ROI”).
Export individual values generated by roi.sh and vol.sh as a comma-separated value (.csv) file using the “Export as CSV” option.
Visualize images generated in future steps, such as those generated by zscore.sh and afni_roi.sh, in the same manner to assess for statistical outliers.
Smooth z-score files using BioImage Suite with a sigma factor of 3.
Resample smoothed images by a factor of 2 × 2 × 2.
Place smoothed and resampled z-score files into subfolders within the folder named afni_roi, distinguished by genotype: hom_smoothed_rsp, het_smoothed_rsp, and wt_smoothed_rsp.

Concatenate the smoothed and resampled files within each subfolder using biswebnode concatenateimage to output a concatenated file (*_concatenation.nii.gz) for each genotype in the respective *_smoothed_rsp folders.
Run 3D t-test (3dttest++) on the concatenated files to establish voxels of fluorescence intensity that are statistically significant between experimental and control groups.
Generate a residual file representing the difference between the data values of the comparison group from the set mean.

Generate a six-frame t-test file using the command: `3dttest++ -prefix ${dttest_folder}/${genotype}_vs_wt_roi_ttest_${div_type}.nii.gz -resid ${dttest_folder}/${genotype}_vs_wt_roi_resid_${div_type}.nii.gz -setA ${sm_folder}/${genotype}_concatenation.nii.gz -setB ${wt_folder}/wt_concatenation.nii.gz -toz`
Estimate the approximate spatial noise distribution of the data using the residual file generated in the 3dttest step.

Use the `3dFWHMx` command to perform spatial autocorrelation on the residual file: `3dFWHMx -input ${dttest_folder}/${genotype}_vs_wt_roi_resid_${div_type}.nii.gz -mask ${ZBRAIN_BINARY_FILE} -acf -detrend`
Copy the output of the 3dFWHMx command to a new file: `cp 3dFWHMx.1D`
Execute the command NUMBER=$(tail -1 ${dClustSim_folder}/${genotype}.num | awk '{print $1, $2, $3}') in the terminal.
Run 3dClustSim with the specified parameters.
Remove files 3dFWHMx.1D and 3dFWHMx.1D.png using the rm command.
Load the standard reference fish (standard_ref.nii.gz) into the BioImage Suite WebApp Viewer Tool.
Load the t-test file generated in Step 13c as an overlay in the viewer tool.
Select “Extract Frame” from the “Image Processing” drop-down menu.
Scroll to the “Extract Frame” tab in the “Viewer Controls” menu.
Type "1" into the “Frame” box and select “Execute” button to extract Frame 1.
Edit advanced settings.
Save the Frame 1 file by selecting “Overlay” → “Save Overlay.”
Load the Frame 1 file (∗roi_ttest_Frame_001_C0divC1.nii.gz) into the afni_roi folder.
Label each experimental group Frame 1 file with the naming convention: experimentalgroup_vs_wt_roi_ttest_Frame_001_C0divC1.nii.gz.
Check for two subfolders (C0divC1, C2divC1) and the Frame 1 file in the afni_roi folder.
Perform cluster filtering using values generated by AFNI and the BioImage Suite WebApp Viewer Tool locally.
Execute the bash script, clusterfilter.sh.
Open the terminal and change directories to the experiment folder.
Type bash clusterfilter.sh followed by the desired p-value threshold number.
Run the script with an example command like bash clusterfilter.sh 0.05.
Thresholded files will appear in a subfolder called thresholded.
Create the experiment folder to generate statistical files for brain volume.
Enter the command line: bash afni_vol.sh wt het hom.
Set PWD to the base name of the current working directory.
Specify BINDIR as the path containing all files and scripts.
Define ZBRAIN_BINARY_FILE as "Zbrain_binary_mask_rsp.nii.gz".
Assign GENO_TYPE based on genotype inputs (e.g., heterozygous, homozygous, wild-type).
Remove 'wt' from GENO_TYPE if present.
Use afni_vol.sh to generate z-score files and perform smoothing steps in Bioimage Suite.
Place generated files in the subfolder afni_vol, separated by genotype.
Do not downsample volume images as they are already downsized for computational feasibility.
Use the BioImage Suite WebApp Overlay Viewer locally to visualize both activity/cell-specific marker cluster-filtered images and z-scored volume images.
Select the “Orthogonal” tab in the Overlay viewer.
Load the standard reference image (File → Load Image → standard_ref_rsp.nii.gz).
Load the Frame 1 image cluster-filtered at the appropriate threshold (Overlay → Load Overlay → ∗Frame_001_C0divC1.nii.gz).
Load the standard reference image in "Viewer 1" using File → Load Image → standard_ref_rsp.nii.gz.
Load the Frame 1 image as an overlay in "Viewer 1" using Overlay → Load Overlay → *Frame_001_C0divC1.nii.gz or *volume_ttest_Frame_001.nii.gz.
Set the Min and Max values for thresholding as described above for the Overlay/Orthogonal Viewer.
Load the standard reference image in Viewer 2 (File → Load Image → standard_ref_rsp.nii.gz).
Load the atlas file as an overlay in Viewer 2 (File → Load Overlay → Zbrain_atlas_149region.nii.gz).
Select “Objectmap” for the “Overlay Type” under the drop-down menu, “Overlay Color Mapping,” in Viewer Control 2.
No Min/Max adjustments are required in “Viewer Control 2.”
